_comment: Provenance for every bundled sample. If you add a file here you MUST fill these fields. 'bands_are_physically_valid' = false means: do NOT compute NDVI/NDWI from it and present the result as vegetation/water measurement.

RGB.byte.tif.name: Landsat-derived 8-bit RGB subset (rasterio test fixture)
RGB.byte.tif.what_it_is: A 3-band 8-bit GeoTIFF (~300 m pixels, EPSG:32618) distributed as test data with the rasterio project. It is real satellite imagery, but the upstream acquisition date/sensor is not documented in the file itself.
RGB.byte.tif.notes: 8-bit display-scaled values; the red band here is a visible-red band, NOT a red-edge or NIR band. Use it to prove the pipeline runs, never to prove an NDVI value.

all-nodata.tif.name: 4-band uint16 surface-reflectance-style scene, entirely nodata
all-nodata.tif.what_it_is: 71 x 2475 px, 4 bands (blue, green, red, nir), uint16, 3 m pixels, EPSG:32628. GDAL metadata shows a 6S atmospheric-correction record dated 2022-01-17. Every pixel is nodata (=0).
all-nodata.tif.notes: This is our regression test for 'statistics must not silently count nodata pixels'. Any stat computed on it must report 0 valid pixels, not a mean of 0.0.

byte.tif.name: Single-band 8-bit raster, EPSG:26711 (NAD27 / UTM 11N)
byte.tif.what_it_is: 20 x 20 px, 1 band, uint8, 60 m pixels, no nodata declared. A classic rasterio test fixture.
byte.tif.notes: Useful because its CRS is NAD27 (EPSG:26711) -- it proves we really transform datums instead of assuming everything is WGS84.

rotated.tif.name: Rotated (non-north-up) raster, no CRS
rotated.tif.what_it_is: 10 x 15 px, 1 band, uint8. Affine transform has non-zero rotation terms (b, d) and the file has NO CRS.
rotated.tif.notes: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE, not satellite imagery. Exists to prove the app degrades gracefully instead of drawing a wrong footprint.

float_nan.tif.name: 3x2 float32 raster with NaN nodata and no CRS
float_nan.tif.what_it_is: 3 x 2 px, 1 band, float32, nodata = NaN, no CRS, suspicious Y resolution.
float_nan.tif.notes: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE. Guards against NaN-vs-nodata confusion, which will matter a lot when we divide by (NIR + Red) in Phase 3.

rgb1_fake_nir_epsg3857.tif.name: 8-bit raster in EPSG:3857 (name is misleading)
rgb1_fake_nir_epsg3857.tif.what_it_is: 676 x 681 px, 1 band, uint8, ~200 m pixels in EPSG:3857 Web Mercator. Despite the filename, this file ships with ONE band upstream, so it provides no real NIR.
rgb1_fake_nir_epsg3857.tif.notes: Kept deliberately: it is a live reminder never to trust filenames or band counts as evidence of band meaning.

s2_s2b-36ruv-20230806-0-l2a_2048px.tif.name: Sentinel-2 L2A MGRS-36RUV window (2023-08-06)
s2_s2b-36ruv-20230806-0-l2a_2048px.tif.what_it_is: Real Copernicus Sentinel-2 MSI Level-2A surface-reflectance window: 2048x2048 px at 10 m (20.5 km), 4 bands (B02 blue, B03 green, B04 red, B08 nir), uint16 DN, EPSG:32636, nodata=0. Extracted from the AWS Open Data COG archive.
not_good_for: change detection (only one date is bundled)
s2_s2b-36ruv-20230806-0-l2a_2048px.tif.notes: Reflectance = DN/10000. The STAC raster:bands metadata advertises offset -0.1, but applying it makes ~98% of pixels negative, so BOA_ADD_OFFSET is 0 for this baseline (verified empirically -- see docs/PHASE2.md). Bands 1-4 are NOT in wavelength order: order is blue, green, red, nir.

s2_s2b-36ruv-20230118-0-l2a_2048px.tif.name: Sentinel-2 L2A MGRS-36RUV window (2023-01-18)
s2_s2b-36ruv-20230118-0-l2a_2048px.tif.what_it_is: Real Copernicus Sentinel-2 MSI Level-2A surface-reflectance window: 2048x2048 px at 10 m (20.5 km), 4 bands (B02 blue, B03 green, B04 red, B08 nir), uint16 DN, EPSG:32636, nodata=0. Cut from the SAME pixel window as s2_s2b-36ruv-20230806-0-l2a_2048px.tif, so the two scenes share one CRS, affine transform and shape.
not_good_for: cloud-covered pixels are not masked (scene-wide cloud is 0.061131); no atmospheric correction beyond L2A
s2_s2b-36ruv-20230118-0-l2a_2048px.tif.notes: Reflectance = DN/10000 (BOA_ADD_OFFSET 0, verified empirically -- see docs/PHASE2.md). Band order is blue, green, red, nir -- NOT wavelength order. Acquired by the same sensor and processing level as the reference scene to keep the comparison like-for-like.
